quote.translation: We cannot say "all B are A", only, as a particular judgement, "some B are A", because, as the signs b ≮ a′ or b ≠ ba′ show, room remains for contingency to intervene between A and B. We can say, for example, "all members of the yellow race are human", but we cannot say "all humans are members of the yellow race"; changing the universal into a particular judgement, we can say only "some humans are members of the yellow race".

quote.translation: The skin colour that marks racial difference is a contingent mark of the concept of the human, and so long as this categorical contingency lies hidden within it, the only course open is to use the particular judgement, as a conversion "by accident".
